item.description: - Hydro's 446 million dollar loss is its worst in years, driven by the fourth drought year in five, debt now above 26 billion. - Diesel at 2.64 a litre is up 60 per cent since before the Iran war, and those costs are already showing up in freight and grocery pricing. - per cent of Winnipeggers back the police drug crackdown, a live issue heading into the October 28th civic vote. - River Heights-Fort Garry will get its first new councillor in 17 years, three names to watch. - Reconciliation Day drew huge crowds at the Forks and in Brandon, and the province is now acquiring the Brandon burial site campground.

item.title: 2026-10-01 Canadian Politics: Trump's Trade Lesson, Aitchison Exits, Quebec's Crown Fight
item.description: - Trump calling Canada "the worst of any country" is rhetoric, but the tariffs on alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles are real and already in effect. - A twelfth Conservative MP resignation since January means more by-elections and more churn in this Parliament. - Eyre's comments suggest Ottawa wants to keep defence ties with Washington intact even as trade ties fray. - Conservatives want immigration targets cut further just as Carney talks about eventually raising them again, a live debate for housing demand. - Quebec's PQ wants to sever ties to the Crown, but the constitutional path looks genuinely uncertain.

item.title: 2026-10-01 Climate Policy & Nonprofit Governance: Permitting Deal and Diesel Crisis Reshape Energy Policy
item.description: - The Senate permitting bill could reshape how energy projects get approved nationwide, but passage is not guaranteed. - Diesel prices and Hormuz related costs are driving major fiscal and political pressure in both the US and EU. - Governance fights are intensifying, from UK disclosure rules to pressure campaigns against researchers to habitat offset policy in Canada.

item.title: 2026-10-01 AI & Technology: OpenAI Launches AI Agents as Industry Faces Scrutiny
item.description: - OpenAI's Dev Day introduced Dots, cute AI agent mascots, alongside new models GPT-6 Astra and the budget-friendly GPT-6.1 Sol. - Analysts question whether OpenAI's agent push addresses real safety concerns following hacking incidents tied to AI agents. - Amazon and Meta are clashing over AI shopping agent Muse, with Walmart taking the opposite stance from Amazon. - Meta disputes a report that its Muse agent accessed private messages without user permission. - Google released Gemini 4 Argon, its latest flagship model, aimed at coding and cybersecurity. - Bank of England's Andrew Bailey warned AI investment could pose risks to financial markets while cautioning against premature regulation.

item.title: 2026-10-01 Health & Fitness: Tendon Training, Gut Bacteria, and the Science of Fear
item.description: - Tendon pain responds better to added load than to pure bodyweight work, and the exact percentage matters less than once thought. - Isolation moves like leg extensions can fix cheating on compound lifts during rehab. - Mulberry and gut bacteria research looks promising but is still animal studies, not proven in humans. - Moderate, voluntary stress, even a scary hike, may train the same calm under pressure skills as exposure therapy. - Basic emergency readiness is a resilience habit, not a paranoia habit.

item.title: 2026-10-01 Parenting: Manitoba Child Care Hits $10 Hard Cap
item.description: - Manitoba's 10 dollar a day child care now covers kids up to age 12, ahead of most provinces. - Ontario and Alberta still sit well above that 10 dollar figure, worth modelling into client budgets. - Paediatric allergy guidance still says introduce allergen foods around 6 months, not later. - EI parental leave choice, 55 percent over 40 weeks versus 33 percent over 69, changes a household's cash flow plan. - RESP grant money, 20 percent on the first 2,500 dollars a year, is easy to leave on the table.

item.title: 2026-10-01 Sports: Jets Open Friday, Bombers Fight for Playoff Life
item.description: - Jets host Boston Friday at seven, first home test since the Hellebuyck exit. - Bombers at 7 and 7, big measuring-stick game Saturday against first-place Montreal. - Leafs finally won one, but the McKenna rookie season will be a slow build. - Watch the Stanley Cup final TV fight, Canadians could lose free over-the-air access. - Chiefs and Raiders both unbeaten, Sunday's game decides first loss bragging rights.
